newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: S.Africa's Mandela arrives in Mozambique for talks.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Mandela arrives in Mozambique for talks.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela arrived in the Mozambican capital Maputo on Friday for talks with President Joaquim Chissano.
A Mozambican presidential official said the talks were at the request of Mandela who telephoned Chissano on Thursday night but the official did not know the reason for the meeting.

The two southern African leaders are likely to discuss regional problems including simmering political tension in neighbouring Swaziland and Lesotho and delays in a two-year-old peace process in Angola.
On Thursday Mandela travelled to Zimbabwe for talks with President Robert Mugabe and later flew to Botswana where he met President Sir Ketumile Masire to discuss regional crises.
At the end of the meetings Mandela said collective efforts were necessary to help resolve problems in the region.
In Swaziland unions are heading a drive for political reform through industrial strikes which have crippled its vital sugar and timber export industries.
The government, headed by King Mswati III, ordered the arrest of three of the country's union leaders who still remain in detention, and deployed troops ahead of the national strike on February 3.
In the mountain kingdom of Lesotho, hugged on all sides by South Africa, a group of mutineering policemen have taken control of the police headquarters and called for a national police strike.
